input: Find bribery and corruption allegations involving Embraer, in Brazil and abroad

entity.group: Embraer S.A. — Brazilian multinational aerospace corporation, the third-largest civil aircraft producer after Boeing and Airbus with a top-100 defense contractor ranking; group entities cited in the FCPA case include Embraer Representations LLC (US subsidiary) and ECC Investment Switzerland AG (Swiss subsidiary)
entity.hq_country: Brazil (headquarters: São José dos Campos, São Paulo)

events.type: Foreign bribery / FCPA violations (bribery, false books and records, internal controls)
events.amount: US$205.5 million total: US$107,285,090 DOJ criminal penalty plus approximately US$98.2 million SEC disgorgement and prejudgment interest ($83,848,291 + $14.4M), with up to a $20 million credit for disgorgement paid to Brazilian authorities under a parallel civil proceeding (approximately US$18.2 million — R$58 million to a Brazilian federal fund and R$6 million to the Brazilian CVM)
events.status: settled — three-year deferred prosecution agreement with DOJ and settled SEC civil action; charges to be dismissed with prejudice if DPA not breached
events.parties: Embraer S.A. and its U.S.-based subsidiary Embraer Representations LLC
events.summary: Embraer paid more than US$5.76 million (approximately $6 million) in bribes through third-party agents and false consulting agreements to foreign government officials in the Dominican Republic, Saudi Arabia and Mozambique — reaping over US$83 million in profits on tainted contracts — and ran an improper US$5.76 million payment scheme in India, concealing the payments with false books and records; Embraer did not self-report (the SEC subpoena opened the probe), and an internal investigation led by Baker & McKenzie lasted more than six years.
events.jurisdiction: United States (SEC; DOJ, S.D. Fla., No. 16-cr-60294) and Brazil (MPF/CVM TCAC)

events.date: 2008–2011 (initial $100,000 payment through a corporate shell entity, remainder $3.42 million via a sham consulting agreement purportedly for Jordan)
events.type: Bribery of a foreign government official (Dominican Republic air force)
events.amount: US$3.52 million in bribes to secure Dominican Senate approval of a US$96.4 million (≈$92 million) military aircraft sale (eight Super Tucano light attack planes)
events.status: alleged (company-level); charged against individuals in Brazil — see separate event
events.parties: Embraer S.A. and consultant Elio Moti Sonnenfeld; a then-colonel in the Dominican Republic's air force
events.summary: Embraer paid a $3.52 million commission to a Dominican air force colonel through a shell company and a sham consulting agreement to win Senate approval of an eight-plane Super Tucano sale, per SEC/DOJ settlement documents and Brazilian prosecutor statements.
events.jurisdiction: Dominican Republic (with US and Brazilian parallel proceedings)

events.date: circa 2009 (sale of three E170 business jets worth approximately US$93 million to a Saudi state-owned enterprise, identified in a 2016 WSJ article as Saudi Aramco)
events.type: Bribery of a foreign official / state-owned enterprise executive (Saudi Arabia)
events.amount: US$1.65 million in bribes ($550,000 per jet) funneled through a South African company purportedly for a real estate transaction; US-gathered evidence spurred additional investigations by Saudi authorities
events.status: alleged at company level; convicted against former Embraer executive Colin Steven in the US — see separate event; two individuals were also charged in Saudi Arabia
events.parties: Embraer S.A.; former Embraer VP of sales Colin Steven; Mazen Snobar (Saudi Aramco employee)
events.summary: Embraer paid $1.65 million through a phony consulting agreement to a Saudi Aramco executive to win a roughly $93 million jet sale, and US, Brazilian and Saudi authorities opened a global investigation of the individuals involved.
events.jurisdiction: Saudi Arabia (prosecuted in the United States and Saudi Arabia)

events.date: circa 2009–2010 (sale of two E190 commercial jets to state-owned airline Linhas Aéreas de Moçambique, S.A. for approximately US$65 million)
events.type: Bribery / corrupt payment to a foreign government official (Mozambique)
events.amount: US$800,000 sham consulting agreement ($400,000 per airplane)
events.status: alleged — resolved within the company's 2016 global settlement
events.parties: Embraer S.A.; a company related to a Mozambican national; a Mozambican government official
events.summary: Embraer executed a $800,000 sham consulting agreement with a company related to a Mozambican national at the behest of a Mozambican government official as a condition of obtaining the LAM state-airline contract.
events.jurisdiction: Mozambique (investigation assisted by the South African Financial Services Board)

events.date: 2008 (sale of three specialized military surveillance aircraft to the Indian Air Force for US$208 million)
events.type: Improper payments / FCPA books-and-records and internal controls violations (India)
events.amount: approximately US$5.76 million paid under a false agency agreement
events.status: alleged — resolved in the 2016 US settlement; Indian authorities opened a corruption investigation into kickbacks from the air force contract
events.parties: Embraer S.A., ECC Investment Switzerland AG, and an agent affiliated with an Indian national
events.summary: Embraer caused its Swiss subsidiary to pay $5.76 million under a false agency agreement with a company affiliated with an Indian national, to circumvent Indian law prohibiting commercial agents for military sales, and falsely recorded it as a consulting agreement.
events.jurisdiction: India (payment routed via Embraer's Swiss subsidiary, ECC Investment Switzerland AG, through a UK-based company)

events.date: 2014 (criminal complaint); charges against Sonnenfeld dismissed February 2017
events.type: Criminal corruption and money laundering charges against former executives and consultant (Dominican Republic deal)
events.amount: US$3.4 million received by Sonnenfeld from Embraer for work he did not perform, passed along as a bribe to a Dominican public official
events.status: charged — Brazilian prosecutors filed a criminal complaint in 2014 against Sonnenfeld and eight former Embraer vice presidents, directors and managers; a Brazilian judge dismissed the charges against Sonnenfeld in February 2017 (outcome for the other eight not stated in available sources)
events.parties: Consultant Elio Moti Sonnenfeld and eight former Embraer vice presidents, directors and managers; CEO Frederico Curado was named by the consultant as allegedly aware but never charged or accused
events.summary: Brazilian prosecutors charged the sales consultant and eight former Embraer executives with corruption and money laundering over the Dominican Republic aircraft deal, though the judge later dismissed the charges against Sonnenfeld.

events.type: FCPA violations, wire fraud, money laundering and conspiracy — individual prosecution of a former Embraer executive
events.amount: US$1.65 million payment arranged to a Saudi Aramco employee, plus a US$130,000 kickback Steven arranged to himself
events.status: convicted — pleaded guilty; at sentencing after a five-year investigation the court ordered only forfeiture and a small fine, with no jail or probation, rewarding his cooperation
events.parties: Colin Steven, 61, former Embraer vice president of sales
events.summary: Former Embraer sales VP Colin Steven pleaded guilty in SDNY to arranging the $1.65 million bribe to a Saudi Aramco employee via a South African company to secure the sale of three E170 jets worth about $93 million, and received no jail time in return for his cooperation.
events.jurisdiction: United States (U.S. District Court, Southern District of New York)

output.assessment: Embraer's corruption exposure centers on the 2016 FCPA global settlement — US$205.5 million paid to US DOJ, SEC and Brazilian authorities for bribery in the Dominican Republic, Saudi Arabia and Mozambique plus an improper-payment scheme in India — resolved via a three-year DPA whose independent monitor found in April 2020 that Embraer's compliance program was reasonably designed and implemented, with the monitorship expiring May 22, 2020. Individual enforcement continued afterward (the 2017 guilty plea of former sales VP Colin Steven), and the 2014 Brazilian criminal complaint's outcome for the eight former executives is unclear from available sources. No new company-level bribery or corruption enforcement action against Embraer surfaced for 2024–2026 in the sources reviewed, so residual risk is mainly the unconfirmed final dismissal of the deferred charges and any still-open foreign (India, Saudi Arabia) investigations.
missing_fields: Confirmation that the DOJ formally dismissed the criminal charges when the three-year DPA expired (post-May 2020) — the 2020 20-F states the intent but a later confirmation is not in the retrieved pages
Final outcome of the 2014 Brazilian criminal complaint against the eight former Embraer executives (other than the February 2017 dismissal of charges against Sonnenfeld)

excluded_namesakes.name: Eve Air Mobility
excluded_namesakes.reason: eVTOL company listed among Embraer's subsidiaries/affiliates; a separately managed entity, not the subject of any bribery allegation found — any adverse news about it was excluded as not concerning Embraer S.A.'s conduct

excluded_namesakes.name: Rolls-Royce plc
excluded_namesakes.reason: UK engine maker that settled its own separate corruption case with US, Brazilian and UK authorities in 2016–2017 (over $800 million); it co-appears in the same FCPA review pages as Embraer but is a distinct company with no ownership link
